page: Microsoft Azure M48s_1_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv3 family, managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs based on an Intel x86_64 architecture and supplies 974.0 GB of system memory. This resource distribution yields an extreme memory density of approximately 20.29 GB per core, accommodating workloads requiring large addressable memory spaces relative to CPU compute capacity.

Hardware capabilities do not include local disk storage or attached graphics processing units, as local storage is none and GPU count is zero. The instance is designed for Premium Storage support, requiring remote managed storage volumes for OS and data persistence. Furthermore, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included, requiring virtual network routing or auxiliary network attachments for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the architecture emphasizes high memory capacity per compute unit rather than raw storage bundling or accelerator density. Deployments that require massive in-memory footprints without needing high processor-to-memory ratios will minimize overhead compared to deploying wider compute configurations. This specification profile is suited for large relational database management systems, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning suites, and memory-intensive analytics engines.
description: Microsoft Azure M48s_1_v3 is a memory-optimized instance from the MSMediumMemoryv3 family, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It delivers 974.0 GB of memory, providing an extensive memory-to-core allocation of 20.29 GB per vCPU. The server lacks local storage and GPU hardware, operating entirely with external Premium Storage options for disk I/O requirements, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Designed for memory-centric enterprise applications, the M48s_1_v3 provides significant RAM capacity relative to its compute core count, making it well matched for in-memory databases, large-scale database management systems, enterprise ERP deployments, and large-footprint analytical workloads.
